name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,776

entries.clue: Anticipate chopping all wood (6)

indicatorNotes.chopping: chopping ALL cuts those letters away from the word

blocks.note: to forestall = to anticipate and get in first
the letters A, L, L are cut away from the end of the word

annotation.surface: Someone expects a lumberjack to fell every tree in a wood.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'chopping' sound like tree-felling, which suits the wood; in fact it chops the letters ALL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name land covered with trees, the answer usually the larger.

entries.clue: Principal in favour of some turning up on time (8)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, turning up turns SOME upside down, so it reads upwards

annotation.surface: A head teacher supports some pupils who arrive punctually.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a vague quantity word, but it is the very letters to be turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: Foremost means first in rank, principal.

entries.clue: Lots of oil here on fancy clothes (8)

annotation.surface: An actor slathers oil on an elaborate costume.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym: a refinery is a place where lots of oil is.
annotation.definitionFit: A refinery is where crude oil is processed, so there is lots of it there.

entries.clue: Love god rebuffed by Romeo becomes increasingly irritated (5)

annotation.definitionNote: SORER is a comparative adjective: more irritated

indicatorNotes.rebuffed: rebuffed = pushed back, so the god's name goes backwards

blocks.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
Romeo is R in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Cupid, snubbed by Romeo, gets crosser and crosser.
annotation.walkthrough: Romeo seems to belong with the love god in a romantic story, but he only supplies the letter R.
annotation.definitionFit: Sorer means more irritated, as in a sorer temper.

entries.clue: However stock rotates, one's behind (8)

indicatorNotes.rotates: rotates moves STOCK's first letter round to the end

blocks.note: STOCK with its S moved to the back

annotation.surface: A trader shrugs that whichever way the shares go, somebody lags behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like the market loser trailing the pack; here it is the noun, your rear.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with 'behind' as the informal noun for the rear and 'one's' standing for anyone's.

entries.clue: Heavy metal, you said? (7)

indicatorNotes.said: said means spoken aloud, so 'you' gives the letter that sounds like it

annotation.surface: Someone checks they heard right that you are into heavy metal music.
annotation.walkthrough: U is the chemical symbol for this element, so the sound 'you' leads to its full name. 'Heavy metal' looks like the music genre.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: one of the densest metallic elements, used as nuclear fuel.

entries.clue: Call them regularly and help out United (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly: regularly takes every other letter of THEM
indicatorNotes.out: out = in disorder, so HELP ONE is rearranged

blocks.note: first and third letters of THEM

annotation.surface: A plea to phone some people from time to time and help Manchester United.
annotation.walkthrough: United looks like the football club, but it gives ONE, as in people who stand united as one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to call someone is to ring them up.

entries.clue: Underground chamber opening in California state institution at last (6)

indicatorNotes.opening in: the opening of California is its first letter
indicatorNotes.at last: institution at last is its final letter

annotation.surface: A cave opens up beneath a California state prison.
annotation.walkthrough: 'California state' reads as one phrase, but state is a verb here, AVER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names a large cave, a chamber under the ground.

entries.clue: They're often dressed as revolutionary youths (6)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: revolutionary = turning over, so AS goes backwards

annotation.surface: Young people often dress up as revolutionaries, Che Guevara T-shirts and all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' suggests clothes and costumes; salads are dressed with oil and vinegar. 'As' looks like a link word but is part of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Salads are typically served with a dressing.

entries.clue: Becomes parody, as last of employees is demoted (4,2)

indicatorNotes.is demoted: in a down clue, demoted sends the S lower down the word

blocks.note: final letter of employees, the S at the top of SEND UP, moved down three places

annotation.surface: A satirical sketch shows the last worker being moved to a lower post.
annotation.walkthrough: The S that starts SEND UP drops from the top of the grid entry to below END, giving END S UP.
annotation.definitionFit: To end up as something is to become it in the end.

entries.clue: Arbitrator earned suspect votes (9)

indicatorNotes.suspect: suspect = dubious, so EARNED is jumbled

annotation.surface: An adjudicator won dubious ballots, hinting at a rigged election.
annotation.walkthrough: The plural REFERENDA, not referendums, matches the plural 'votes'.
annotation.definitionFit: Referenda are public votes on single questions.

entries.clue: Demolish stable and flat (5)

blocks.note: to raze a building to the ground
steady and even, as a head or a voice can be
flat and horizontal, like a billiard table

annotation.surface: Instructions to knock down a stable and a flat.
annotation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'stable' and 'flat' pose as buildings to be demolished but are adjectives.
annotation.definitionFit: A triple definition: a verb meaning raze, and an adjective meaning both steady and horizontal.

entries.clue: One might take ore fragment from seam in error (5)

indicatorNotes.fragment from: a fragment from the phrase is a run of its letters

annotation.surface: A mistaken dig pulls a chunk of ore out of the seam.
annotation.walkthrough: The mining picture hides the answer in its own words; 'fragment' sounds like a lump of rock but points to part of the text.
annotation.definitionFit: A miner is someone who extracts ore.

entries.clue: Controlled ship, stuffed initially with preserved fish (9)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially takes the first letter of stuffed

blocks.note: kippered = cured by smoking, as herrings are

annotation.surface: A captain ran a vessel packed with smoked fish.
annotation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, and KIPPERED describes fish preserved that way.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun for a ship's captain used as a verb, in the past tense to match 'controlled'.

entries.clue: Party involved in drink fiasco (5-2)

indicatorNotes.involved in: involved in = wrapped inside, so CREW sits within SUP

blocks.note: a crew = a party, a group

annotation.surface: A group mixed up in some drunken debacle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a drinks do, but it is a group of people, CREW.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for a botched job, from the slang verb meaning to bungle.

entries.clue: With a start, he's held up inside store (9)

indicatorNotes.held up: in a down clue, held up raises HE so it reads upwards

blocks.note: to rouse = to start up from sleep
HE written upwards, placed inside ROUSE

annotation.surface: A man jumps in fright after being held up at gunpoint in a shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With a start' reads as a phrase about a fright, but it is three separate pieces: W, A and ROUSE. 'Held up' suggests a robbery.
annotation.definitionFit: A warehouse is a building where goods are stored.

entries.clue: Reveal 4 - low number (4)

blocks.note: to low = to moo, as cattle do

annotation.walkthrough: 4 is 4 across, BUTTOCKS: to moon is to show your bare bottom as a prank. 'Low' is the verb for a cow's call.
annotation.definitionFit: Mooning means baring your buttocks to someone.

entries.clue: Milk supplier sure went crazy (3,5)

indicatorNotes.went crazy: crazy tells us to jumble; the fodder is SURE WENT

annotation.surface: A dairy farmer was certain and then lost his mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Milk supplier' suggests a dairy or milkman; a wet nurse breastfeeds another woman's baby.
annotation.definitionFit: A wet nurse is a woman employed to breastfeed another's child.

entries.clue: Two sons' 24 adhesive labels (8)

indicatorNotes.24: 24 across is TAKE HEART: the two sons take (contain) heart, TICKER

blocks.note: ticker = heart, the thing taken inside the sons

annotation.walkthrough: Read 24 across, TAKE HEART, as an instruction: S and S take a heart, TICKER, between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the self-adhesive labels children collect and put on things.

entries.clue: A bird shedding hard patch (4)

indicatorNotes.shedding: shedding drops the H from RHEA

blocks.note: a rhea is a large flightless South American bird
h = hard, shed from RHEA to leave REA

annotation.surface: A bird moulting leaves a bald patch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shedding' suggests moulting feathers, but the bird sheds a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a patch of ground is a bounded piece of space.

entries.clue: Cook starts to appreciate making a nice pasty (7)

indicatorNotes.Cook: to cook the books is to rearrange them; cook jumbles the letters
indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of appreciate and making are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of appreciate and making

annotation.surface: Instructions to bake a pasty that will be appreciated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like the Cornish pastry, a pasty; here it is the adjective, pale and unhealthy-looking.
annotation.definitionFit: Anaemic means pale and sickly, pasty-faced.

entries.clue: Can we hear stew cooking? It's a life-saver (3,4)

indicatorNotes.hear: hear says CAN as its synonym MAY sounds, spelt MAE
indicatorNotes.cooking: cooking stirs STEW into new order

blocks.note: can = may, as in may I?
STEW anagrammed gives WEST; WE plus ST completes it

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether they can hear the stew bubbling, which will save their life.
annotation.walkthrough: A Mae West is an inflatable life jacket, named after the buxom film star.
annotation.definitionFit: The Mae West life jacket saved airmen who ditched at sea.

entries.clue: Monstrous dog devours a knight (6)

indicatorNotes.devours: devours = swallows, so MUTT goes around A N

blocks.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: A fearsome hound gobbles up a knight in armour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Monstrous' seems to describe the dog but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Mutant can describe something monstrously altered, as in mutant creatures.

entries.clue: One with purse covered in gold, returned in perfect state (6)

indicatorNotes.covered in: covered in gold puts AU around the other pieces
indicatorNotes.returned: returned sends the whole result back, reading upwards in this down clue

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a pot = a purse, a pool of prize money

annotation.surface: A rich person with a gold-covered purse comes home, which is paradise.
annotation.walkthrough: A-I-POT-U is built first, then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Named after Thomas More's 1516 book about an ideal island commonwealth, hence any perfect state.

entries.clue: Key void in piece of space-station (6)

indicatorNotes.void: void = empty, so KEY loses its middle letter
indicatorNotes.in: in, read literally, means placed inside: KY is set within the letters of SLAB

blocks.note: a slab = a piece, as of cake
KEY emptied of its inner letter

annotation.surface: Looking for a missing key part on a space station.
annotation.walkthrough: Skylab was the first US space station, launched in 1973.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one particular space-station, the first American one.

entries.clue: Organise the karate rally (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Organise: organise = arrange, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An order to set up a martial-arts gathering.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rally' looks like a noun, a meeting, but it is the verb: to recover spirit.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to rally in spirit, to cheer up after a setback.

entries.clue: First of murderers - Cain - wild and frenzied (5)

indicatorNotes.First of: first of murderers is its first letter
indicatorNotes.wild: wild means out of control, and letters that run wild no longer keep their order, so CAIN is rearranged

annotation.surface: Cain, the first murderer in the Bible, is described as wild and frenzied.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wild and frenzied' reads as a pair of adjectives, but wild is the anagram instruction and only frenzied is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Manic means frenzied, wildly overexcited.

entries.clue: Little kid picked up strength (5)

indicatorNotes.picked up: picked up = heard, as by a microphone

annotation.surface: A small child was lifted by someone strong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' paints a child being lifted; here it means caught by ear.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: power and strength, as in 'with all his might'.

entries.clue: Girl regularly entertained by French city's spicy dish (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: regularly takes every other letter of girl
indicatorNotes.entertained by: entertained by = hosted within, so IL goes inside PAU

blocks.note: Pau is a city in south-west France
second and fourth letters of GIRL

annotation.surface: A young woman is treated to a spicy meal by a French city.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in city's belongs to the surface only; the definition follows it.
annotation.definitionFit: Pilau is spiced rice cooked in stock, often with meat.

entries.clue: Animals here include badger between outskirts of Milwaukee and Great Lake (9)

indicatorNotes.between: between puts NAG in the gap between ME and ERIE

blocks.note: Lake Erie, one of North America's Great Lakes

annotation.surface: Wildlife around Milwaukee and a Great Lake includes the badger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like one of the animals, but it is the verb, to pester.
annotation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of animals kept for show.

entries.clue: Bee flying with 25A feeling (8)

indicatorNotes.flying: flying = scattered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: 25 across is MANIC, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A bee buzzing about in a frenzy.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies letters rather than meaning: MANIC joins BEE in the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the mood or atmosphere a place gives off, the feeling in the room.

entries.clue: Behead bears? Not us (6)

indicatorNotes.Behead: behead cuts off the first letter

blocks.note: to mother = to give birth to, as to bear does; its M is removed

annotation.surface: A gruesome command to decapitate bears, with a hasty disclaimer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animal but is the verb, gives birth to, which in Chambers is also what 'mothers' means.
annotation.definitionFit: Defined by contrast: the people who are not us.
